135-001.r: Shatt-al-Arab → Basra; Paraguay river → Asuncion; Niger → Niamey; Danube → Vienna.

135-002.r: Paris → Seine; Kinshasa → Zaire (Congo); Bangkok → Chao Phraya; Asuncion → Paraguay river.

135-003.r: Wrong: Sydney – Seine (the Seine flows through Paris). Correct: Khartoum → Nile (White and Blue Nile meet); New York → Hudson; Berlin → Spree.

135-004.r: Washington D.C. → Potomac; Berlin → Spree; Paris → Seine; Madrid → Manzanares.

135-005.r: Paris → Seine. Belgrade → Danube and Sava; Lisbon → mouth of the Tagus; Budapest → Danube.

135-008.r: Berlin → Spree; Lahore → Ravi; New York → Hudson; Rome → Tiber.

135-009.r: Wrong: Berlin – Rhine; Berlin is on the Spree. Correct: London → Thames; New York → Hudson; Vienna → Danube.

135-010.r: Wrong: Vienna – Volga; Vienna is on the Danube. Correct: Bonn → Rhine; Cairo → Nile; New York → Hudson.

135-011.r: Correct pair: Budapest → Danube. Others: Paris → Seine; Perth → Swan; Cairo → Nile.

135-012.r: Not matched: New Orleans is on the Mississippi (not Missouri); Hyderabad on the Musi (not Paleru). Budapest–Danube and Cologne–Rhine are correct.

135-013.r: Correct: Hamburg → Elbe. Others: Belgrade → Danube (not Seine); Kiev → Dnieper (not Don); Lahore → Ravi (not Satluj).

135-014.r: Rome → Tiber, not the Danube. Capitals on the Danube: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade.
135-014.h: Danube capitals go V-B-B-B: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade.

135-015.r: Huangpu River (113 km) → flows through Shanghai, splitting Pudong (east) from Puxi (west); Shanghai also lies at the Yangtze mouth.

135-016.r: Bangkok → Menam (Chao Phraya); Phnom Penh → Mekong; Hanoi → Red River; Yangon → Irrawaddy.

135-017.r: Potomac → USA; Nile → Sudan; Tigris → Iraq; Thames → England.

135-018.r: Wrong: Lisbon – Tiber; the Tiber (Italy's third longest) flows through Rome into the Tyrrhenian Sea. Belgrade–Danube, Warsaw–Vistula, Washington–Potomac are correct.

135-019.r: London → Thames; Antwerp → Scheldt; Rotterdam → Rhine; Hamburg → Elbe.

135-020.r: Rotterdam → Rhine; Paris → Seine; Budapest → Danube; Washington D.C. → Potomac.

135-021.r: Khartoum → Nile (Blue and White Nile meet); Brazzaville → Zaire (Congo); Rotterdam → Rhine; Paris → Seine.

135-022.r: Watershed (catchment area) → land unit that collects, stores and releases water, channelling rain and snowmelt to streams, rivers, reservoirs and the sea.

136-001.r: Delta formation depends on sea depth: deltas need heavy sediment, slow flow, a gentle sea floor and a shallow sea or shelf; a deep sea hinders them.

136-002.r: World's greatest delta → Ganga-Brahmaputra (Sunderban) delta in Bangladesh and West Bengal; arcuate, triangular, about 105641 sq km.

136-003.r: Bird's foot delta → Mississippi, at the Gulf of Mexico.
136-003.t: Don't confuse: Mississippi = bird's foot delta; Nile = arcuate delta.

136-004.r: Grand Canyon → a gorge cut by the Colorado River in Arizona, USA; about 446 km long and over 1.8 km deep.

136-005.r: Chisapani Gorge → Nepal, cut by the swift Karnali, Nepal's longest river (507 km).

136-006.r: Wrong: Inselberg is not a glacial landform. Correct: Canyon → river; Zeugen → wind; Moraine → glacier (its deposits).

136-007.r: Nobi and Kanto plains → Japan; Kanto (central Honshu, 17000 sq km, holds Tokyo) is Japan's largest lowland.

137-001.r: Sheep Islands → Faroe Islands, a self-governing archipelago of Denmark with 18 rocky, volcanic islands.

137-002.r: Area: NZ South Island (150436 sq km) > Java (138794) > NZ North Island (114687) > Newfoundland (111390).

137-003.r: World's largest island → Greenland (Denmark); then New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar.

137-004.r: Second largest island → New Guinea (785753 sq km, north of Australia), after Greenland. Madagascar → Africa's largest island.

137-006.r: Greenland → world's largest island, belongs to Denmark (not USA); Nuuk is its capital and largest city, 1-3 m above sea level.

137-008.r: Borneo → shared by three countries: Indonesia (73%), Malaysia (26%), Brunei (1%); world's third largest and Asia's largest island.

137-009.r: Area: Borneo (751929 sq km) > Madagascar (587041) > Sumatra (472784) > Great Britain (209331).

137-010.r: Borneo → divided among Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei; formed by volcanic deposition; third largest island after Greenland and New Guinea.

137-011.r: Kalimantan → Indonesian part of Borneo, 73% of the island.

137-012.r: Madagascar → largest island in the Indian Ocean (south-west); Mauritius to its east, Mozambique to its west.

137-013.r: Indian Ocean map: Seychelles → 3; Chagos → 1; Mauritius → 4; Socotra → 2. Seychelles has 155 granite and coral islands.

137-014.r: South Indian Ocean islands: Chagos, Mauritius and Seychelles; the book accepts all three.
137-014.c: The book gives no single answer (*): Chagos, Mauritius and Seychelles all lie in the south Indian Ocean.

137-015.r: Melanesia (western Pacific): Bismarck Archipelago, Fiji, New Caledonia, New Guinea, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu.

137-016.r: Diego Garcia → Indian Ocean; named after a Portuguese explorer; under Mauritius 1814-1965, then UK, leased to USA as a strategic base.

137-017.r: Indonesia → archipelago from Aceh (north-west) to Torres Strait (east); 17508 islands, about 1000 inhabited.

137-018.r: Atlantic map 1-4: Azores (Portugal), Cape Verde, the Bahamas, Falkland (UK).

137-019.r: Falkland archipelago → South Atlantic (about 650 km east of South America), not Indian Ocean. Namibia → Africa; Nicaragua → Central America; Yemen → Asia.

137-020.r: Fiji → South Pacific; 333 islands; Viti Levu and Vanua Levu hold 87% of people; neighbours Vanuatu, Tonga, Tuvalu.

137-021.r: Galapagos Islands (Pacific) → volcanic in origin; belong to Ecuador, not Peru.

137-022.r: Japan's largest island → Honshu (capital Tokyo); four main islands: Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu.

137-024.r: Japan north to south: Hokkaido → Honshu → Shikoku → Kyushu; Tsugaru Strait (Seikan undersea rail tunnel) separates Hokkaido and Honshu.
137-024.h: 'Hot Honey Shakes Kids': Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu.

137-026.r: Macau → transferred from Portugal to China in December 1999; lies about 64 km west of Hong Kong.

137-027.r: Balearic Islands → Spain, western Mediterranean Sea; capital Palma de Mallorca; part of Spain since 1833, autonomous since 1983.

137-028.r: World's largest river island → Majuli, in the Brahmaputra (Assam); first river island made a district in India.

137-029.r: Island continent → Australia, the world's smallest continent.

137-030.r: Grenada → three-island country in the south-east Caribbean Sea, 'Island of Spice', about 160 km north of Venezuela.

137-031.r: Salt-pan resources → Saint-Martin Island; salt pans form in arid areas where water bodies dried up, leaving salt.

137-032.r: Most islands among options → Indonesia (17508); in the whole world, Sweden has the most islands.

137-033.r: Socotra → part of Yemen (not Oman), at the mouth of the Gulf of Aden; UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site in 2008.

137-034.r: Indonesian islands, west to east: Sumatra → Java → Bali → Lombok.

137-035.r: Madeira → not in the Caribbean Sea; Grenada, Montserrat and Anguilla are Caribbean islands.

137-036.r: Polynesia includes Tonga, Tuvalu and Tahiti (French Polynesia); Tinian is not Polynesian.

138-001.r: Lake Faguibine (Mali, West Africa) → dried up and turned into desert.

138-002.r: Wrong: Baikal → Russia, not Ukraine. Correct: Balkhash → Kazakhstan; Titicaca → Bolivia-Peru; Erie → USA-Canada.

138-003.r: Lake Balkhash → east-central Kazakhstan; largest lake in Central Asia.

138-004.r: Niagara Falls → on the Niagara River between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario, on the USA-Canada border.

138-005.r: Lake Tanganyika → second deepest lake (1470 m) after Baikal and the longest freshwater lake.

138-006.r: Equator passes through none of Lake Tanganyika, Lake Tonle Sap and Patos Lagoon; all lie away from 0° latitude.

138-007.r: Great Lakes: Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario; Bear Lake is not one of them.
138-007.h: HOMES: Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, Superior.

138-008.r: Great Lakes east to west: Ontario → Erie → Huron → Michigan → Superior; Lake Michigan lies wholly in the USA.
138-008.h: West to east 'Super Man Helps Every One': Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario.

138-011.r: Lake area: Superior (82097 sq km) > Victoria (68870) > Baikal (31500) > Great Bear (31153).

138-012.r: Size order: Superior (≈82367 km²) > Victoria (≈58016 km²) > Michigan > Chilika.

138-013.r: Largest freshwater lake (by area) → Lake Superior, one of the Great Lakes on the Canada-USA border.

138-014.r: Oldest and deepest lake → Lake Baikal: maximum depth about 1642 m, over 25 million years old.

138-015.r: Lake Baikal → world's oldest and deepest freshwater lake (1642 m deep, over 25 million years old).

138-016.r: Deepest lake → Baikal (Siberia, Russia; 1642 m). Titicaca 280 m; Victoria maximum 84 m.

138-017.r: Largest lake by area and volume → Caspian Sea (Eurasia), a saltwater lake of about 371000 km².

138-018.r: Finger Lakes region → series of small lakes in north-west New York, USA.

138-019.r: Garden of Lakes → Finland (about 187888 lakes, 178917 islands); its largest lake, Saimaa, is Europe's fourth largest.

138-020.r: Land of a thousand lakes → Finland.

138-021.r: Wrong: Five Flower Lake → Sichuan, China, not Mongolia. Correct: Boiling Lake → Dominica; Red Lagoon → Bolivia; Great Slave Lake → Canada.

138-022.r: Duluth → on the shore of Lake Superior (second largest city on it).

138-023.r: Wrong: Reindeer Lake → Canada, not Russia. Correct: Titicaca → Bolivia-Peru; Urmia → Iran; Athabasca → Canada.

138-024.r: Highest waterfall → Angel Falls (Salto Angel), Venezuela, 979 m, on Rio Churun (Orinoco system); Tugela Falls (South Africa) 948 m.

138-026.r: Victoria Falls → Zambezi River, on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

138-027.r: Lake Victoria → bordered by three countries (Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya), not four; lies between branches of the East African Rift, not in the rift valley.

138-028.r: Lake Victoria: second (not third) largest freshwater lake by area; borders only Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya (not Rwanda); an African Great Lake; Nile outflow near Jinja.

138-029.r: Plitvice Lakes (Croatia) → UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979; sixteen lakes linked by waterfalls.

138-030.r: Wrong: tallest waterfall is Angel Falls (Venezuela, 979 m), not Tugela (second, 948 m). Correct: Superior, Titicaca (highest navigable), Tanganyika (second deepest).

138-031.r: Wrong: Lake Malawi → Africa, not Asia. Correct: Baikal → Russia; Caspian → Asia-Europe; Tanganyika → Africa.

138-032.r: Aral Sea → shrunk almost dry from human activity (NASA images 2014 vs 1989); Black Sea and Baikal shrank only slightly.

138-033.r: Wrong: Lake Onega → north-west Russia (Europe's second largest after Ladoga), not Canada. Correct: Maracaibo → Venezuela; Michigan → USA; Baikal → Russia.

139-001.r: Strait of Malacca (between Indonesia and Malaysia) → links Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) with South China Sea.

139-002.r: India–East Asia sea route could be cut most by a new canal between the Gulf of Siam and the Andaman Sea, not by deepening Malacca Strait.

139-003.r: Strait of Gibraltar → separates Europe from Africa; joins the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea.

139-004.r: Strait of Hormuz → between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.

139-005.r: Strait of Hormuz → connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman; vital oil route from West Asia.

139-006.r: Bering Strait (85 km wide) → separates Asia (Russia) from North America (Alaska); links Chukchi Sea (Arctic) with Bering Sea (Pacific).

139-007.r: Suez Canal → greatest economic and strategic weight; cut Europe-India distance by 7000 km; about 12% of world trade. Bering Strait links Arctic and Pacific.

139-009.r: Gibraltar → Africa-Europe; Malacca → Indonesia-Malaysia; Bering → Asia-North America; Hormuz → Persian Gulf-Gulf of Oman.

139-010.r: Ten Degree Channel → separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands (Bay of Bengal); named for the ten-degree north latitude.

139-011.r: UK-France tunnel → under Strait of Dover, Folkestone (Kent) to Coquelles (France); Dover Strait joins English Channel and North Sea.

139-013.r: Palk Strait → between Tamil Nadu (India) and Sri Lanka; Palk Bay lies between Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal; named after Robert Palk.

139-015.r: Persian Gulf countries: Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Iraq. Oman borders the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea instead.

139-017.r: Correct: Gulf of Tonkin → Vietnam (and China). Gulf of Bothnia → Finland-Sweden; Baffin Bay → Canada-Greenland; Gulf of Carpentaria → northern Australia.

139-018.r: Bab-el-Mandeb → links Red Sea with Indian Ocean (Gulf of Aden). Hormuz → Persian Gulf-Gulf of Oman; Bosphorus → Black Sea-Sea of Marmara.

139-019.r: Lombok Strait → between Bali and Lombok (Indonesia); joins the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean.

139-020.r: Devil's Neck → Kra Isthmus (southern Thailand and Myanmar), narrow land joining the Malay Peninsula to mainland South-East Asia.

139-021.r: Bass Strait (about 240-350 km wide) → separates Tasmania from mainland Australia (Victoria).

140-001.r: Suez Canal (Egypt, 193.30 km, opened 1869) → joins Mediterranean and Red Sea; Port Said (north), Suez (south); largest navigation canal; shortened India-West route.

140-005.r: Suez Canal → directly joins the Red Sea and Mediterranean Sea (not the Atlantic or Indian Ocean); cut India-Europe sea distance by about 7,000 km.

140-007.r: Bombay to Suez port needs no Suez Canal transit, since Suez port lies at the canal's southern end.

140-008.r: Panama Canal → cut across the Isthmus of Panama; joins Atlantic and Pacific Oceans; shortened New York-San Francisco sea route.

140-009.r: Soo Canal → joins Lake Superior and Lake Huron (Great Lakes of North America).

140-010.r: Nicaragua → planned a rival to the Panama Canal linking Atlantic and Pacific (announced October 4, 2006; about US$18 billion, about 12 years).

140-011.r: Kiel Canal (Germany) → joins the North Sea and Baltic Sea; one of the busiest artificial waterways.

140-012.r: Locks raise and lower ships between water levels; the book names the Panama Canal and Danube River among lock-operated waterways in the options.
140-012.c: The book gives no single answer (*): more than one option uses a lock system.

140-013.r: Ludwigs Canal → inland waterway of southern Germany. Volga-Don Canal → Russia; White Sea Canal → White Sea to Lake Onega; Sault Ste. Marie → Canada.

140-014.r: Kiel → Elbe estuary-Baltic Sea; Soo → Lake Superior-Lake Huron; Panama → Atlantic-Pacific; Suez → Mediterranean-Red Sea.

140-015.r: Suez Canal lakes, north to south: Lake Manzala → Lake Timsah → Great Bitter Lake → Little Bitter Lake.
140-015.h: 'Many Tourists Get Lost': Manzala, Timsah, Great Bitter, Little Bitter.

141-001.r: Itaipu Dam → on the Parana, joint project of Brazil and Paraguay; 196 m high, 7919 m long.

141-002.r: Jiaozhou Bay Bridge (China) → among the world's longest sea bridges, 41.58 km, Qingdao to Huangdao; opened 30 June 2011.

141-003.r: Colorado → Hoover Dam; Damodar → Panchet (Hill); Nile → Aswan; Zambezi → Kariba.

141-004.r: Kariba Dam → Zambezi River, on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

141-005.r: Aswan High Dam → Egypt, on the Nile; used for irrigation and hydropower; construction began in 1960.

141-006.r: Zangmu Dam → China's gravity dam on the Yarlung Zangbo (Brahmaputra) in Tibet, begun Nov. 2010; may reduce the river's flow.

141-007.r: Wrong: Hoover (Boulder) Dam → Colorado River (Nevada-Arizona), not Tennessee. Correct: Grand Coulee → Columbia; Nurek → Vakhsh; Cahora Bassa → Zambezi.

142-001.r: Coral reefs → mostly in coastal waters between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn; cover 0.08-0.16% of oceans but hold 25% of marine species.

142-002.r: Great Barrier Reef → world's largest coral reef, in the Pacific off Queensland (north-east Australia); about 2300 km long.

142-003.r: Great Barrier Reef → north-east coast of Australia (Queensland), Pacific Ocean; about 2300 km long, so 'more than 2500 km' is wrong.

142-007.r: Most coral reefs are tropical; over one-third lie in Australia, Indonesia and Philippines; reefs host more animal phyla than tropical rainforests. All three true.

142-008.r: Addu Atoll → Indian Ocean; the southernmost atoll of the Maldives.

142-009.r: Atoll → ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef island enclosing a lagoon; found in tropical and subtropical seas.

143-001.r: Dust is higher in subtropical and temperate areas than equatorial and polar ones because dry winds are more common there; so Statement II is false.

143-002.r: Troposphere is much thicker at the equator than at the poles because strong convection carries heat high; both true, II explains I.

143-003.r: Near-surface air is mainly nitrogen (78.084%) and oxygen (20.947%); the remaining 1% is argon, carbon dioxide, neon etc. Most abundant gas → nitrogen.

143-005.r: Permanent gases (steady amount): nitrogen, oxygen, argon. Carbon dioxide, ozone and neon vary.

143-006.r: Layers upward: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Ionosphere (lower thermosphere) → Exosphere.
143-006.h: 'The Strong Man Is Energetic': Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Ionosphere, Exosphere.

143-007.r: Lowest layer → troposphere (average height about 12-13 km); all weather such as rain, fog and hail occurs in it.

143-011.r: Most weather occurs in the troposphere; its temperature falls 6.5°C per 1000 m (1 km) of height.

143-013.r: Jets fly in the stratosphere because its dry air has almost no clouds or weather disturbances.

143-014.r: Ozone layer → lower stratosphere, mainly 15-35 km up (up to 55 km); absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays.

143-016.r: Ozone layer → blocks the Sun's ultraviolet rays; lies in the lower stratosphere, mainly 15-35 km up (also asked as 15-20 km); ozone = three oxygen atoms.

143-020.r: Ionosphere → reflects (deflects) radio waves; cosmic rays are identified and auroras seen in this layer.

143-021.r: Aurora Borealis (north) and Aurora Australis (south) → in the ionosphere, 80-640 km up; light from charged solar particles hitting the atmosphere.

143-022.r: Ionosphere's charged particles (ions) reflect radio waves back to Earth, enabling wireless communication and telecommunication.

143-024.r: Communication (geostationary) satellites → about 36000 km up, in the exosphere (outer atmosphere above 640 km).

143-025.r: Correct: Troposphere → weather; Stratosphere → ozone layer; Ionosphere → reflects radio waves. Wrong: Mesosphere – aurorae (aurorae belong to the ionosphere).
